stickies.text: When both Home lists are empty: ONE small combined hint line replaces both sections — never two big icons. Bottom action bar in the reader auto-hides on scroll down, returns on scroll up.

PROPOSAL (revision 5): Topic mode during search. Search -> a topic card appears under the field (5+ results). Tap -> topic capture: top 12 results ranked by CENTRALITY (how many other candidates link to each one). Majority-linked = CORE, pre-checked; PERIPHERAL = unchecked, tap to override. Depth + images chips reuse per-save options. Name is editable.

PROPOSAL (revision 6): LONG-PRESS a search result -> ANCHORED DROPDOWN at the finger — never a slide-up sheet. Rows: Read now / Save offline (submenu) / Add to topic / Open on Wikipedia. Tap still opens the article; bookmark icon stays quick-save. Ripple on every tappable row is required.

S1 PURPOSE: show, at a glance and in plain words, how the app gets built and shipped and where everything stands right now — so the maintainer knows what’s what, what’s going on, what needs them, and where to go next.

S2 AUDIENCE: the maintainer is primary (daily "where do things stand / what needs me" check on a phone); curious public-app users are secondary, reading it as a story of how the ecosystem is built. Everything shown must be public-safe — counts, dates, generic labels only, no session tags, branch names, commit subjects, hosts, or ops details.

S3 IN SCOPE: Home entry (purpose line, Right now card, Needs you list, three named doors) · Story door (What’s new, Timeline, Releases) · System door (System map, Versions & pipeline, Applets board, House rules) · Reference door (process boards, widget/package reference, unchanged content re-housed). Data comes from automated mirror snapshots, asOf-stamped.

S4 OUT OF SCOPE v1: no editing from the applet (no writes to ledgers/boards); no live/streaming data (snapshots only, honest "as of"); no cross-applet live reads (engine ask, queued); no internal ops console features (those stay in the private aidev/Dispatch channel).

S5 RULES: every screen answers the four questions (What is this? What’s going on? What do I do? Where do I go?); ≤4 named doors, words never icon-only; one purpose line per screen, no legends/paragraphs on group headers; no truncation; one switcher style everywhere; small detail = popup, substantial = full-screen push, never a bottom sheet.

S6 DONE MEANS: a new visitor can say what the applet is, what’s happening, and what to do within 10 seconds on a phone, without tapping. Every screen passes the four-question test and the layout/public-safety gates. Screenshots of every screen reviewed by the maintainer on dev before prod.
D1 DECISION NEEDED: is the secondary audience (public readers) in, or maintainer-only? Affects how much of the ship pipeline gets shown. RECOMMEND: public-in, public-safe data only.
D2 DECISION NEEDED: Home’s "Needs you" actions — link-out only (open the relevant screen) or real one-tap actions (e.g. "mark seen")? RECOMMEND: link-out only for v1.
D3 DECISION NEEDED: order of the three doors — Story · System · Reference (recommended) or System first? RECOMMEND: Story · System · Reference, story-first reads better for a new visitor.

KIND GAP (Story door): no native `spine`/`timeline` widget kind exists in composer today — the Time spine example uses `list` as the closest real kind. A dedicated spine kind (areas down, time sideways, HERE marker per the scope doc’s Timeline sub-view) would need an engine round.

KIND GAP (System door): no native `table`/`matrix` widget kind exists in composer today — the Dev|Prod example uses `list` as the closest real kind. A true 2-column matrix (web/app × dev/prod, per the scope doc’s Versions & pipeline sub-view) would need an engine round.
